anomalies.observed: On the FCC Peripherals sheet the PWM driver U14 (PCA9685PW) has all six address-select pins A0-A5 (pins 1-6) tied to GND, giving a 7-bit address of 0x40. On the Power sheet the current/voltage sensor U9 (INA219AIDCNR) also has A0/A1 tied to GND, giving 0x40. Both devices are wired to the same FCC I2C bus: U14 SCL=NET0099/SDA=NET0108 and U9 SCL=NET0099/SDA=NET0108. The PWM-driver block's own text note reads 'I2C address: 0x41', i.e. the intended strapping leaves A0 high, but the drawing straps it low.
anomalies.expected: The two devices must have distinct addresses on the shared FCC I2C bus so the FCC can drive the PWM/servo driver and read the current/voltage sensor independently (spec §1: FCC 'drives a PWM servo driver, reads a current/voltage sensor'). The schematic's own note specifies 0x41 for the PCA9685, so A0 (pin 1) should be pulled high, not tied to GND.

evidence.quote: FCC Peripherals, PWM Driver block: 'I2C address: 0x41' while pins 1-6 (A0-A5) are drawn connected to GND
Power sheet, U9 INA219AIDCNR: 'I2C address: 0x40', pins 7/8 (A0/A1) to GND, SCL=NET0099, SDA=NET0108; U14 SCL=NET0099, SDA=NET0108
FCC 'drives a PWM servo driver, reads a current/voltage sensor' (§1) - both must be individually addressable on the FCC I2C bus

anomalies.impact: I2C address collision: the PCA9685 PWM driver and the INA219 power monitor respond to the same address 0x40 on the same bus (NET0099/NET0108). The FCC cannot communicate with both reliably; servo/PWM output and battery current/voltage telemetry would fail or be corrupted.

parsed.summary: The build matches the spec on part numbers, crystal values, regulator/shunt values and the documented barometer pin-swap bug, but the PWM driver U14 is strapped to I2C 0x40 (all address pins grounded) while sharing the FCC bus NET0099/NET0108 with the INA219 U9 at 0x40, contradicting the sheet's own '0x41' note and the requirement that both be addressable - an I2C address collision.
